title: POC: hosting vs dedicated vs private - prioritization & benchmarks (Lynx Retail)
summary: Discovery / scoping call for a 6-week pilot. Lynx wants to validate hosted vs dedicated vs private for an in-store assistance chat and inventory QA workload. Primary priorities: sub-100ms 95p latency on short-turn chats, predictable throughput at peak store traffic (target 250 qps), and strict data residency + KMS-based encryption. Agreed to run a synthetic benchmark and a 500-prompt evaluation set; Redwood to deliver pricing, pilot runbook, and security pack.
transcript:
[00:00] Eve Carter (Redwood AE): Hey all, thanks for joining — we goal to cover scope, success metrics, timeline for the pilot. Micah and Samir are with me to answer infra and perf qs.
[00:11] Tara Singh (Lynx): Thanks, Eve. Quick context: we run chat-based in-store assistant and an inventory reconciliation job. We have spikes during weekend noon-2pm. We need high confidence on latency and cost for black friday kind-of load, but initial pilot is for 6 weeks.
[00:28] Jon Park (CTO): Also, security — the retail data includes PII and some vendor contracts require data residency in us-west. So VPC/private is something we might need.
[00:41] Micah Lin (Redwood SE): Got it. Two workloads then: interactive chat (short sessions, average 20 tokens out, maybe 60 tokens exchange) and batch reconciler (larger context, 2-5k tokens). We'll size both.
[00:55] Avery Gomez (Infra): For baseline, what's the expected concurrency for chat? Is it per store or aggregated?
[01:02] Marisol Vega (Product): Aggregate across 1,200 stores. Peak per-store is small, aggregate peaks we see ~250 concurrent chat requests.
[01:12] Micah: OK, 250 qps peak. For hosted mode, we can handle that with autoscaling but there are warm-up considerations for KV cache and cold starts. Dedicated gives pinned capacity and consistent latency; private gives VPC + on-prem options for data residency but more ops.
[01:35] Tara: Our success criteria — shorthand: 95th percentile latency <100ms for chat, 99th percentile not more than 200ms, throughput sustain 250 qps for 10 minutes, and reconciliation jobs must complete within 20 minutes for a full batch. Cost target: not to exceed $X per million tokens (Tara hesitates) — we'll give a budget range of ~ $1,500-2,500/month for pilot infra not counting integration work.
[02:05] Eve: Helpful. We typically propose a three-phase pilot: planning & security checks (week 0-1), benchmark + integration (week 2-4), evaluation + handoff (week 5-6). We run synthetic benchmarks and also use your 500 prompt eval set.
[02:20] Jon: What's the delta on instrumentation between hosted and dedicated for observability? We need token-level cost and per-route latency traces.
[02:30] Samir Patel (Redwood SA): Same telemetry surface — our Console exposes token spend per-route, latency histograms, and traces. Dedicated gives you private metrics retention options and longer retention for enterprise. Private (VPC) can pipe logs into your Splunk/Elastic but requires some ops configuration.
[02:49] Avery: About encryption, we need customer-managed keys. KMS integration?
[02:53] Micah: Yes — KMS/HSM support in Private and Dedicated for enterprise accounts. Hosted can support customer-managed keys for payload at rest via managed KMS in supported regions, but for full HSM you'd want Private.
[03:10] Marisol: Can you give an example bench run we could expect on hosted vs dedicated for the chat workload?
[03:16] Micah: Rough ballpark: Using a 7B-class open model optimized with quantization, you'd see ~70-120ms 95p on dedicated with warmed KV cache and continuous batching tuned for short chats. Hosted can be similar for steady loads but might spike higher during cold starts. Private on customer's infra depends on their HW; on equivalent GPUs you'd match dedicated.
[03:43] Tara: We care about cost predictability — dedicated reserved capacity seems attractive if we commit. We have to assess commit vs variable usage.
[03:51] Eve: Right. For dedicated we offer reserved pools with burst capacity. For pilot we can provision a small dedicated pool with month-to-month flex to validate.
[04:03] Jon: Bench methodology? Do you require us to provide sample logs/session traces?
[04:08] Samir: We request a 500-prompt eval set for output quality checks and a short synthetic load file that mirrors your token distribution. We'll run 30-minute sustained runs at target concurrency and collect 95/99 percentiles, token/sec, and cost per 1k tokens.
[04:26] Tara: On the reconciliation batch job, we need to feed in 1.2M lines — how do you benchmark that?
[04:33] Micah: We simulate the job with the same average sequence lengths, parallelize across workers; measure wall-clock time. If you want, we can sample a 10% subset to iterate faster.
[04:45] Marisol: Are there tradeoffs in quality for faster quantized runtimes? We need to maintain NLU accuracy for our slot-filling and item normalization.
[04:54] Micah: Yes slight regressions possible with aggressive quantization. Redwood Optimize recommends quant profiles by workload and will flag potential delta on your eval set. We can run evals at FP16 and at int8 to show differences.
[05:07] Jon: What about fallback policies? If the model variant fails under load do you have automatic fallbacks?
[05:12] Samir: Yes, smart routing can fallback to a lower-cost variant or to a simpler heuristic service; you can set SLO thresholds. We can demo routing rules in the pilot.
[05:22] Tara: Network egress concerns — if hosted, does any payload leave our region? We need to ensure data residency in us-west.
[05:30] Eve: Hosted offers regional endpoints; for strict residency and contractual requirements, Private (VPC/on-prem) is recommended. Dedicated can be region pinned too. We'll map options to your compliance needs in the security pack.
[05:45] Avery: For the pilot, we need a checklist: SOC2 docs, data flow diagrams, SAML/SSO config, KMS notes.
[05:52] Eve: We'll share a security-pack.pdf and an architecture diagram. Also a pilot-scope-lynx.xlsx with timeline and benchmark plan.
[06:02] Tara: Timeline clarifications: we want a pilot ready in 3 weeks if possible — is that realistic?
[06:08] Eve: 3 weeks is aggressive but doable if you provide eval set and infra access quickly. More conservative is 6 weeks.
[06:15] Micah: Key path: share eval prompts + representative traffic, set up credentials, agree on dedicated sizing or hosted region, run baseline bench, iterate.
[06:26] Marisol: Who owns deployment on our side? Avery will lead infra, I will coordinate product requirements.
[06:31] Avery: Yep, I'll be the infra lead. We'll need Redwood runbook for VPC peering steps if we go private.
[06:38] Eve: Action items we'll capture. Any other blockers?
[06:42] Jon: Licensing/compliance sign-off — procurement will need terms, but we can run pilot under an evaluation MSA.
[06:49] Tara: Wanted to confirm the success criteria again so we can sign off internally: 95p chat latency <100ms, sustained 250 qps, reconciliation job within 20m, no outbound data leaving us-west, and SSO + KMS in place.
[07:03] Eve: Affirm. We'll put those as pilot success criteria in the runbook.
[07:08] Micah: Quick note on benchmark numbers we'll produce: 95p/99p latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens, model output diff metrics on your eval set (BLEU-ish / semantic similarity).
[07:22] Marisol: For the 500-prompt eval, we need guidance on formatting.
[07:26] Samir: We'll share a template file. CSV with prompt, expected behavior, and acceptance criteria.
[07:33] Tara: Any concerns about scale beyond pilot — if this goes prod and we need 2k qps how does that change things?
[07:40] Micah: You'd likely move to Dedicated or a hybrid with Dedicated for peak and Hosted for burst across regions. Autoscaling policies and smart routing can optimize cost. We'll include scale pathways in the pilot report.
[07:52] Jon: Are there any known infra blockers for our stack — we run on GCP us-west1 primarily with private VPCs and strict firewall rules.
[08:01] Samir: We can work with GCP and set up VPC peering or Private Service Connect for Dedicated/Private. For hosted we use regional endpoints reachable over TLS; we need an allowlist for outbound to Redwood endpoints.
[08:16] Tara: Okay, let's talk numbers. What does an initial dedicated pool cost for our pilot request?
[08:22] Eve: We'll provide three options in the pricing sheet: small reserved pool sized for 250 qps, medium for 500 qps, and a pay-as-you-go hosted run. For the small dedicated pilot, monthly committed estimate around $6k-$9k depending on GPU class — exact numbers in the spreadsheet.
[08:41] Marisol: We'll need to show procurement a line-item for instrumentation and professional services if integration needed.
[08:47] Eve: We'll include an estimate for 40 hours of Redwood SE time for integration and benching.
[08:53] Tara: Perfect. Any technical risks we should call out?
[08:57] Micah: Main risks: cold-start spikes for hosted, slight quality regression with aggressive quantization, and network egress/residency edge cases. We mitigate via dedicated pools, quant profiles, and VPC options.
[09:12] Jon: Sounds good. Let's recap next steps.
[09:15] Eve: Agreed.
[09:17] Micah: I'll run a short design doc for bench methodology.
[09:20] Tara: Great.
[09:22] Eve: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the security pack, pricing sheet, pilot runbook and the template for eval prompts.
[09:30] [call ends]
